lines.en: Leo, you look upset. What happened while I was waiting for you outside the library?
lines.pt: Leo, você parece chateado. O que aconteceu enquanto eu esperava você na frente da biblioteca?

lines.en: I was walking along Queen Street when I realised my wallet had disappeared from my jacket.
lines.pt: Eu andava pela Queen Street quando percebi que minha carteira tinha sumido do casaco.

lines.en: Had you taken it out before? Maybe you left it in the coffee shop where you had been having lunch.
lines.pt: Você tinha tirado antes? Talvez tenha deixado na cafeteria onde estava almoçando.

lines.en: I checked there first. The waiter said nobody had handed in a wallet, so I started to panic.
lines.pt: Olhei lá primeiro. O garçom disse que ninguém tinha entregado uma carteira, então comecei a entrar em pânico.

lines.en: Then what did you do? I would have called the bank immediately.
lines.pt: E o que você fez? Eu teria ligado para o banco imediatamente.

lines.en: I did call the bank to cancel my cards, and while I was talking, a woman came up and asked if I was Leo.
lines.pt: Eu liguei para o banco para cancelar os cartões, e enquanto falava, uma mulher se aproximou e perguntou se eu era o Leo.

lines.en: No way! She had found the wallet on a bench, and she had recognised you from your ID photo.
lines.pt: Não acredito! Ela tinha achado a carteira num banco e tinha reconhecido você pela foto do documento.

lines.en: Exactly. She had been looking for me for an hour, because the only address inside was an old one.
lines.pt: Isso. Ela vinha me procurando havia uma hora, porque o único endereço lá dentro era antigo.

lines.en: That is incredible. Did she say how it had ended up on the bench?
lines.pt: Que incrível. Ela disse como a carteira tinha ido parar no banco?

lines.en: A boy had picked it up from the pavement after it had fallen out, and he had given it to her.
lines.pt: Um menino tinha pegado da calçada depois que ela caiu, e entregou a ela.

lines.en: What a lucky day. Next time, keep it in a zipped pocket, and thank that woman properly.
lines.pt: Que dia de sorte. Da próxima vez, guarde num bolso com zíper e agradeça direito àquela mulher.

facts.label: Narrativa no passado
facts.sub: Principais eventos: passado simples. Cenário: was walking. Fato anterior: had disappeared. Conecte com when, while, after e before.

facts.label: Passado simples
facts.sub: Use o passado simples para os eventos que fazem a história andar: A woman came up and asked my name. Cada verbo é um passo novo da história. Conte-os na ordem em que aconteceram.

facts.label: Passado contínuo
facts.sub: Use was/were + -ing para o fundo da cena ou uma ação em andamento: I was walking along Queen Street when I saw her. A ação curta interrompe a ação longa, com when.

compare.br: Em português, “tinha sumido” (mais-que-perfeito) é raro na fala; usamos o pretérito.
compare.us: Em inglês, o past perfect marca com clareza o que veio antes: had disappeared.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: The past perfect shows an earlier past action.
We say “I realised my wallet disappeared before”.
Was walking gives the background of a story.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: The past perfect shows an earlier past action. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “I realised my wallet disappeared before”. → Falso (We say had disappeared.)
Was walking gives the background of a story. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A wallet comes home · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a warm afternoon in the centre of Brisbane. People walk along Queen Street with shopping bags. Boris is waiting outside the library. His friend Leo arrives late, and his face is red. Something strange has happened to him. Boris wants to hear the story in order.

“Leo, you look upset. What happened while I was waiting for you outside the library?” says Boris. “I was walking along Queen Street when I realised my wallet had disappeared from my jacket.” says Leo. “Had you taken it out before? Maybe you left it in the coffee shop where you had been having lunch.” says Boris.
